issues.description: The evaluator rejects the expert golden solution (golden_rejected). The golden run fails with a compile error in submission/recovered_rtl.v, indicating the evaluator is buggy or grades the wrong file. This makes the benchmark unusable as-is.
issues.evidence: Validation report differential.golden_run.stdout shows: [TEST] FAIL: FR1: compile failed: submission/recovered_rtl.v:51: syntax error; ...

issues.description: The testbench contains a syntax error at line 178 that causes compilation failure even for the vulnerable baseline. This prevents any simulation from running and makes all requirements untestable.
issues.evidence: Validation report differential.vulnerable_run.stdout: [TEST] FAIL: FR1: compile failed: evaluation/tb_mac_top.v:178: syntax error; ...

issues.description: All six requirements (FR1-FR4, SR1-SR2) are untested because no targeting mutants were provided, so harness discrimination is unproven. The mutation score is 0.0.
issues.evidence: Validation report: untested_requirements: [FR1, FR2, FR3, FR4, SR1, SR2], mutation_score: 0.0

issues.description: The testbench uses a continuous comparison block that may produce false FAIL markers (MISC) even when explicit checks pass, potentially confusing result parsing.
issues.evidence: tb_mac_top.v lines 178-185 contain an always block that prints [TEST] FAIL: MISC on any mismatch, which could interfere with requirement-level pass/fail determination.

issues.description: The public README mentions 'saturation' and 'two-cycle latency' explicitly, which is acceptable, but the example scenarios are quite detailed and could reduce the reverse-engineering challenge. No hidden security intent is leaked.
issues.evidence: README.md includes explicit arithmetic examples and saturation scenarios.

recommendations: Fix the syntax error in evaluation/tb_mac_top.v at line 178. The continuous comparison block should be corrected or removed to allow compilation.
Fix the syntax error in submission/recovered_rtl.v (the shipped baseline) so that it compiles but fails functional simulation, enabling the evaluator to reject it.
Ensure the golden solution (golden/recovered_rtl.v) compiles and passes all tests when used as the submission.
Provide targeting mutants for each requirement to prove harness discrimination and achieve a non-zero mutation score.
Consider adding evaluation of word_recovery_rate and structural_match_accuracy metrics if they are required, or remove them from the specification if only functional equivalence is graded.
Remove or gate the continuous MISC comparison block to avoid spurious FAIL markers that could confuse the result parser.

requirement_results.evidence: The golden solution fails to compile due to a syntax error in the shipped submission/recovered_rtl.v, and the testbench itself has a syntax error. The expected outputs cannot be verified.
requirement_results.requirement: Coherence of public inputs, hidden ground truth, and expected outputs

requirement_results.evidence: Both golden and vulnerable runs fail with compile errors. The evaluator cannot distinguish a correct submission from the baseline because neither compiles.
requirement_results.requirement: Evaluator accepts correct submission and rejects baseline

requirement_results.evidence: The evaluator only checks functional equivalence via simulation. It does not compute word_recovery_rate or structural_match_accuracy as specified in the evaluation metrics.
The requirement_map in the tester bundle explicitly separates FR1-FR4 (functional) and SR1-SR2 (security) with distinct detection strategies.
requirement_results.requirement: Requirement map covers functional and security requirements separately

requirement_results.evidence: The testbench includes vectors for timing invariance (SR1) and extreme signed values (SR2), but the syntax error prevents execution, so activation cannot be confirmed.
All files are standard Verilog and Python; no external dependencies beyond iverilog. No malicious code or network access.
requirement_results.requirement: Task artifacts are self-contained and safe

requirement_results.evidence: The task involves recovering behavioral RTL from an obfuscated gate-level netlist, which is a realistic hardware reverse-engineering scenario.
requirement_results.requirement: Benchmark is adapted to the hardware_reverse_engineering domain

requirement_results.evidence: The syntax error in the testbench and the golden rejection mean no simulation results can be obtained, making the benchmark completely unverifiable.
requirement_results.requirement: No gaps that would make results unverifiable

requirement_results.evidence: README.md and metadata.json contain only public functional requirements. No CWE IDs, SR IDs, threat model, or security-spec documents are exposed.
requirement_results.requirement: No leakage of hidden security intent in public artifacts

requirement_results.evidence: FR1-FR4 specify compilation, reset behavior, basic arithmetic with exact values, and saturation with exact limits. Each is verifiable through the defined interface.
requirement_results.requirement: Public functional requirements are concrete and machine-checkable
